thread_text:
ISSUE #90402: Prompt injection: external content in web_fetch _meta field bypasses EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT wrapper
Author: Udjin79
Date: 2026-06-04T15:51:23Z
Labels: P2, impact:security
State: closed

[c0]
## Summary

External page content fetched via web_fetch can be injected into the _meta field of the tool result without the EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT wrapper or security notice that protects the main text/markdown payload. A crafted page can embed a tool_call block in this unwrapped field, attempting to get the agent to execute a follow-up tool call.

## What happened

While fetching a JS-rendered page (the main body came back nearly empty), the tool result contained an _meta entry whose content field held external page text with an embedded tool_call block requesting a follow-up web_fetch. The embedded block is external page content masquerading as a legitimate agent-issued tool call.

## Root cause

The main text/markdown payload from web_fetch is correctly wrapped in a SECURITY NOTICE plus EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT block. But the _meta.*.content field carries external page content without any wrapper or untrusted marker. One field of the same tool result is sanitized; another is not. Inconsistent trust boundary.

## Impact

- Prompt-injection vector that bypasses the existing untrusted-content guard.
- Any external fetch that populates _meta can attempt to drive agent tool calls via this unwrapped channel.
- The purpose of the EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT wrapper is defeated if a parallel field skips it.

## Expected behavior

Any field in a tool result that can contain external/untrusted content should get the same treatment as the main payload: wrapped in EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT with the security notice, or stripped of model-actionable structures (e.g. tool_call blocks) before being surfaced to the model.

## Notes

- The injection was ignored by the agent; no unintended tool call was executed.
- Reported from a real session (web_fetch on a JS-rendered page; beta v2026.6.x build train).

[c1] @clawsweeper 2026-06-04T15:53:04Z:
Thanks for the context here. I did a careful shell check against current `main`, and this is already implemented.

Current main and the shipped v2026.6.1 tag already close the reported trust-boundary gap: web_fetch model-visible text is wrapped, provider fallback fields are normalized through a whitelist, and transcript-only toolResult.details are stripped before provider conversion.

So I’m closing this as already implemented rather than keeping a duplicate issue open.

<details>
<summary>Review details</summary>

Best possible solution:

Keep the shipped web_fetch wrapping, provider-payload whitelisting, and LLM-boundary details stripping in place; broader prompt-injection architecture can continue in the existing security design discussions.

Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue?

No high-confidence current-main reproduction remains. Source inspection shows web_fetch content fields are wrapped or discarded, and toolResult.details are removed before provider conversion.

Is this the best way to solve the issue?

Yes. The current fix is at the right boundary: normalize web_fetch provider output before returning it and strip transcript-only details before anything crosses the LLM provider boundary.

Security review:

Security review cleared: Current main and v2026.6.1 already wrap or remove the reported untrusted web_fetch side-channel content before it reaches model input.

AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant.

What I checked:

- **Current web_fetch wrapping:** Current main wraps web_fetch text with wrapWebContent/wrapExternalContent and wraps title/warning fields through wrapWebFetchField. ([`src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts:215`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3e6978770a82/src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts#L215), [3e6978770a82](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3e6978770a82))
- **Provider payload whitelist:** Provider fallback payloads are rebuilt from known fields; arbitrary provider keys such as _meta are not copied into the returned web_fetch payload, while text/title/warning are wrapped. ([`src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts:335`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3e6978770a82/src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts#L335), [3e6978770a82](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3e6978770a82))
- **LLM boundary strips details:** normalizeMessagesForLlmBoundary calls stripToolResultDetails before provider prompt conversion, and stripToolResultDetails deletes details from toolResult messages. ([`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.ts:17`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3e6978770a82/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.ts#L17), [3e6978770a82](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3e6978770a82))
- **Regression coverage:** Tests cover provider fallback re-wrapping/truncation and confirm toolResult.details with untrusted text is not replayed to the model. ([`src/agents/tools/web-fetch.provider-fallback.test.ts:40`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3e6978770a82/src/agents/tools/web-fetch.provider-fallback.test.ts#L40), [3e6978770a82](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3e6978770a82))
- **Git history provenance:** Blame attributes the current web_fetch wrapping and tool-result details stripping paths in this shallow checkout to commit 1ce11fbf423b2c0fc7be76504af420de447136aa; the current source carries that behavior forward. ([`src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts:215`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ce11fbf423b/src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts#L215), [1ce11fbf423b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1ce11fbf423b))
- **Release provenance:** The v2026.6.1 release commit contains the same web_fetch wrapping and field normalization behavior; diffing v2026.6.1 to current main on the relevant files shows only comment additions for these paths. ([`src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts:215`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2e08f0f4221f/src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts#L215), [2e08f0f4221f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2e08f0f4221f))

Likely related people:

- **Peter Steinberger:** Blame and path history in this checkout attribute the web_fetch wrapping, provider fallback normalization, and tool-result details stripping code to commits by Peter Steinberger. (role: recent area contributor; confidence: high; commits: [1ce11fbf423b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1ce11fbf423b2c0fc7be76504af420de447136aa), [041fab7b7275](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/041fab7b72754847a641c3a464c5111641f6e424); files: `src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts`, `src/agents/session-transcript-repair.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.ts`)
- **Vincent Koc:** The v2026.6.1 release commit containing the fixed behavior is authored/tagged in the local release history by Vincent Koc. (role: release provenance; confidence: medium; commits: [2e08f0f4221f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2e08f0f4221f522b60423ed6ffd83427942b28de); files: `src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts`, `src/agents/session-transcript-repair.ts`)

Codex review notes: model gpt-5.5, reasoning high; reviewed against [3e6978770a82](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3e6978770a8217eb591dc5314615799164f24d06); fix evidence: release [v2026.6.1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.6.1), commit [2e08f0f4221f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2e08f0f4221f522b60423ed6ffd83427942b28de).

</details>

title: Feature: per-agent MCP server scoping in mcp.servers for non-Codex sessions
need_summary: Whether credentialed MCP servers can be scoped to specific non-Codex agents before tool-policy filtering, with the answer anchored to canonical issue #72591 and code/docs references showing current main lacks non-Codex `mcp.servers.*.agents` support.
security_topic: pre-policy MCP server scoping for agent tool boundaries
answer_text:
Close as a duplicate of the older open canonical MCP scoping request; current main still has global non-Codex `mcp.servers` behavior, while the existing `codex.agents` scope is Codex projection only.

Canonical path: Keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/72591 as the canonical place for the additive config shape, security review, and upgrade behavior for pre-policy MCP server scoping.

So I’m closing this here and keeping the remaining discussion on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/72591.
thread_text:
ISSUE #90392: Feature: per-agent MCP server scoping in mcp.servers for non-Codex sessions
Author: podulator
Date: 2026-06-04T15:29:01Z
Labels: P2, impact:security, impact:other
State: closed

[c0]
## Summary

`mcp.servers` entries are currently offered to all agents at session start, regardless of which agents actually need them. The only way to restrict access is via `tools.allow`/`tools.deny` policy, which strips tools *after* they've already been offered — generating noisy `tool policy removed N tool(s)` log entries on every session spawn for every agent that doesn't need those tools.

## Current behaviour

Given a config like:
```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "yfinance-price-tracker": { "transport": "sse", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8767/sse" }
    }
  },
  "agents": {
    "list": [
      { "id": "analena", "tools": { "allow": ["yfinance-price-tracker__*", ...] } },
      { "id": "harvey",  "tools": { "allow": ["read", "write", ...] } }
    ]
  }
}
```

The gateway offers all 17 yfinance tools to **every** agent at session start, then strips them via `tools.allow` policy for the 6 agents that don't need them. Each strip generates a log entry. On a 7-agent setup with a 30-minute heartbeat cron per agent, this produces ~100+ redundant strip events per day.

## What was tried

`mcp.servers.*.codex.agents` — accepted by config validation but has no effect on regular OpenClaw sessions (Codex app-server projection only, as documented).

Per-agent `mcp` block in `agents.list` — rejected by schema validation (`agents.list.6: Invalid input`).

`toolFilter.exclude: ["*"]` — server-level filter, applies to all agents equally, can't be used to scope to a subset.

## Requested behaviour

A way to declare that an MCP server should only be offered to specific agent IDs *before* tool policy filtering. Something like:

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "yfinance-price-tracker": {
        "transport": "sse",
        "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8767/sse",
        "agents": ["analena"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The `codex.agents` concept already exists for Codex app-server projection — this is the same idea extended to the main session tool inventory path.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.5.28
- 7 agents, 1 SSE MCP server scoped to 1 agent via `tools.allow`
- Raspberry Pi arm64, `openclaw-gateway.service` systemd user service

What I checked:

([`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts:1447`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4eb3d1fae941/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts#L1447), [4eb3d1fae941](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4eb3d1fae941))
- **Codex projection is the only agent-scope implementation found:** `buildCodexUserMcpServersThreadConfigPatch` checks `codex.agents` only while projecting user MCP servers into Codex thread config. ([`src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp-codex.ts:45`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4eb3d1fae941/src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp-codex.ts#L45), [4eb3d1fae941](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4eb3d1fae941))

(role: introduced behavior; confidence: high; commits: [06459ca0dfba](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/06459ca0dfba4ca152d2565b6b29efe9f8360b90), [2e08f0f4221f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2e08f0f4221f522b60423ed6ffd83427942b28de); files: `src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts`, `src/agents/bundle-mcp-config.ts`, `src/config/zod-schema.ts`)

thread_text:
ISSUE #90391: [Feature]: Support Custom Sandbox Backends
Author: sjy3
Date: 2026-06-04T15:27:31Z
Labels: enhancement, P3, impact:security
State: closed

[c0]
### Summary

Would OpenClaw consider adding a pluggable sandbox backend abstraction so Docker remains the default, while remote sandbox runtimes can integrate with the existing sandbox tool surface?

### Problem to solve

Without a pluggable sandbox backend, remote sandbox providers usually need to expose separate plugin tools such as `remote_sandbox_exec`, `remote_sandbox_read`, or `remote_sandbox_write`.

This does not preserve the existing OpenClaw sandbox experience across:

- `exec`
- `process`
- file read/write
- `edit`
- `apply_patch`
- sandbox lifecycle commands


### Proposed solution

Introduce a sandbox backend abstraction that keeps the current Docker behavior unchanged, while allowing future backends to be added.

A minimal first step could be:

1. Add an internal `SandboxBackend` interface.
2. Move the current Docker implementation behind `DockerSandboxBackend`.
3. Add a config option such as `sandbox.backend`, defaulting to `docker`.
4. Ensure unsupported or unavailable backends fail closed instead of falling back to host execution.
5. Consider exposing backend registration to plugins after the internal interface stabilizes.


Expected Benefits

- Support remote sandbox runtimes without replacing built-in tools.
- Preserve existing sandbox semantics such as `mode`, `scope`, and `workspaceAccess`.
- Improve production deployment flexibility.
- Keep sandbox boundaries explicit and auditable.
- Avoid teaching the model to use separate remote-specific tools.

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Impact

This proposal only adds a `SandboxBackend` interface abstraction and backend registration mechanism on top of the current sandbox design.

Expected impact:

- Existing sandbox backends and Docker behavior remain unchanged.
- Current sandbox configuration and tool behavior remain compatible.
- New custom sandbox backends can be registered through the new abstraction.
- Existing users do not need to change their setup.
- The implementation should be incremental and low-risk, since it does not replace or remove any current sandbox backend.

need_summary: Whether the reported prompt-injection bypass in web_fetch’s _meta field was already fixed, with the answer anchored to the v2026.6.1 release commit and the cited web_fetch/LLM-boundary source files showing wrapping and stripping behavior.

question_text:
## Summary

External page content fetched via web_fetch can be injected into the _meta field of the tool result without the EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT wrapper or security notice that protects the main text/markdown payload. A crafted page can embed a tool_call block in this unwrapped field, attempting to get the agent to execute a follow-up tool call.
answer_text:
Thanks for the context here. I did a careful shell check against current `main`, and this is already implemented.

Current main and the shipped v2026.6.1 tag already close the reported trust-boundary gap: web_fetch model-visible text is wrapped, provider fallback fields are normalized through a whitelist, and transcript-only toolResult.details are stripped before provider conversion.

So I’m closing this as already implemented rather than keeping a duplicate issue open.
thread_text:
ISSUE #90402: Prompt injection: external content in web_fetch _meta field bypasses EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT wrapper
Author: Udjin79
Date: 2026-06-04T15:51:23Z
Labels: P2, impact:security
State: closed

[c0]
## Summary

External page content fetched via web_fetch can be injected into the _meta field of the tool result without the EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT wrapper or security notice that protects the main text/markdown payload. A crafted page can embed a tool_call block in this unwrapped field, attempting to get the agent to execute a follow-up tool call.

## What happened

While fetching a JS-rendered page (the main body came back nearly empty), the tool result contained an _meta entry whose content field held external page text with an embedded tool_call block requesting a follow-up web_fetch. The embedded block is external page content masquerading as a legitimate agent-issued tool call.

## Root cause

The main text/markdown payload from web_fetch is correctly wrapped in a SECURITY NOTICE plus EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT block. But the _meta.*.content field carries external page content without any wrapper or untrusted marker. One field of the same tool result is sanitized; another is not. Inconsistent trust boundary.

## Impact

- Prompt-injection vector that bypasses the existing untrusted-content guard.
- Any external fetch that populates _meta can attempt to drive agent tool calls via this unwrapped channel.
- The purpose of the EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT wrapper is defeated if a parallel field skips it.

## Expected behavior

Any field in a tool result that can contain external/untrusted content should get the same treatment as the main payload: wrapped in EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT with the security notice, or stripped of model-actionable structures (e.g. tool_call blocks) before being surfaced to the model.

## Notes

- The injection was ignored by the agent; no unintended tool call was executed.
- Reported from a real session (web_fetch on a JS-rendered page; beta v2026.6.x build train).

comments.author: Udjin79
comments.body:
## Summary

External page content fetched via web_fetch can be injected into the _meta field of the tool result without the EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT wrapper or security notice that protects the main text/markdown payload. A crafted page can embed a tool_call block in this unwrapped field, attempting to get the agent to execute a follow-up tool call.

## What happened

While fetching a JS-rendered page (the main body came back nearly empty), the tool result contained an _meta entry whose content field held external page text with an embedded tool_call block requesting a follow-up web_fetch. The embedded block is external page content masquerading as a legitimate agent-issued tool call.

## Root cause

The main text/markdown payload from web_fetch is correctly wrapped in a SECURITY NOTICE plus EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT block. But the _meta.*.content field carries external page content without any wrapper or untrusted marker. One field of the same tool result is sanitized; another is not. Inconsistent trust boundary.

## Impact

- Prompt-injection vector that bypasses the existing untrusted-content guard.
- Any external fetch that populates _meta can attempt to drive agent tool calls via this unwrapped channel.
- The purpose of the EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT wrapper is defeated if a parallel field skips it.

## Expected behavior

Any field in a tool result that can contain external/untrusted content should get the same treatment as the main payload: wrapped in EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT with the security notice, or stripped of model-actionable structures (e.g. tool_call blocks) before being surfaced to the model.

## Notes

- The injection was ignored by the agent; no unintended tool call was executed.
- Reported from a real session (web_fetch on a JS-rendered page; beta v2026.6.x build train).

thread_text:
ISSUE #90392: Feature: per-agent MCP server scoping in mcp.servers for non-Codex sessions
Author: podulator
Date: 2026-06-04T15:29:01Z
Labels: P2, impact:security, impact:other
State: closed

[c0]
## Summary

`mcp.servers` entries are currently offered to all agents at session start, regardless of which agents actually need them. The only way to restrict access is via `tools.allow`/`tools.deny` policy, which strips tools *after* they've already been offered — generating noisy `tool policy removed N tool(s)` log entries on every session spawn for every agent that doesn't need those tools.

## Current behaviour

Given a config like:
```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "yfinance-price-tracker": { "transport": "sse", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8767/sse" }
    }
  },
  "agents": {
    "list": [
      { "id": "analena", "tools": { "allow": ["yfinance-price-tracker__*", ...] } },
      { "id": "harvey",  "tools": { "allow": ["read", "write", ...] } }
    ]
  }
}
```

The gateway offers all 17 yfinance tools to **every** agent at session start, then strips them via `tools.allow` policy for the 6 agents that don't need them. Each strip generates a log entry. On a 7-agent setup with a 30-minute heartbeat cron per agent, this produces ~100+ redundant strip events per day.

## What was tried

`mcp.servers.*.codex.agents` — accepted by config validation but has no effect on regular OpenClaw sessions (Codex app-server projection only, as documented).

Per-agent `mcp` block in `agents.list` — rejected by schema validation (`agents.list.6: Invalid input`).

`toolFilter.exclude: ["*"]` — server-level filter, applies to all agents equally, can't be used to scope to a subset.

## Requested behaviour

A way to declare that an MCP server should only be offered to specific agent IDs *before* tool policy filtering. Something like:

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "yfinance-price-tracker": {
        "transport": "sse",
        "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8767/sse",
        "agents": ["analena"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The `codex.agents` concept already exists for Codex app-server projection — this is the same idea extended to the main session tool inventory path.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.5.28
- 7 agents, 1 SSE MCP server scoped to 1 agent via `tools.allow`
- Raspberry Pi arm64, `openclaw-gateway.service` systemd user service

ISSUE #90391: [Feature]: Support Custom Sandbox Backends
Author: sjy3
Date: 2026-06-04T15:27:31Z
Labels: enhancement, P3, impact:security
State: closed

[c0]
### Summary

Would OpenClaw consider adding a pluggable sandbox backend abstraction so Docker remains the default, while remote sandbox runtimes can integrate with the existing sandbox tool surface?

### Problem to solve

Without a pluggable sandbox backend, remote sandbox providers usually need to expose separate plugin tools such as `remote_sandbox_exec`, `remote_sandbox_read`, or `remote_sandbox_write`.

This does not preserve the existing OpenClaw sandbox experience across:

- `exec`
- `process`
- file read/write
- `edit`
- `apply_patch`
- sandbox lifecycle commands


### Proposed solution

Introduce a sandbox backend abstraction that keeps the current Docker behavior unchanged, while allowing future backends to be added.

A minimal first step could be:

1. Add an internal `SandboxBackend` interface.
2. Move the current Docker implementation behind `DockerSandboxBackend`.
3. Add a config option such as `sandbox.backend`, defaulting to `docker`.
4. Ensure unsupported or unavailable backends fail closed instead of falling back to host execution.
5. Consider exposing backend registration to plugins after the internal interface stabilizes.


Expected Benefits

- Support remote sandbox runtimes without replacing built-in tools.
- Preserve existing sandbox semantics such as `mode`, `scope`, and `workspaceAccess`.
- Improve production deployment flexibility.
- Keep sandbox boundaries explicit and auditable.
- Avoid teaching the model to use separate remote-specific tools.

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Impact

This proposal only adds a `SandboxBackend` interface abstraction and backend registration mechanism on top of the current sandbox design.

Expected impact:

- Existing sandbox backends and Docker behavior remain unchanged.
- Current sandbox configuration and tool behavior remain compatible.
- New custom sandbox backends can be registered through the new abstraction.
- Existing users do not need to change their setup.
- The implementation should be incremental and low-risk, since it does not replace or remove any current sandbox backend.

### Evidence/examples

ISSUE #90377: openclaw sidecar 20260604.2: gateway announces 'ready' before bundled-plugin runtime-dep install, kubelet liveness-kills container (exit 137)
Author: smisy-system-design
Date: 2026-06-04T14:56:19Z
Labels: P1, impact:crash-loop
State: closed

[c0]
## openclaw sidecar `20260604.2` killed by Kubernetes liveness probe after `gateway ready` due to runtime plugin-dep install starving event loop

**Repro context**: nail-notes-api `ai-central` deployment, openclaw running as a sidecar to a Go HTTP server. Pin bumped from `20260521.4` → `20260604.2` today (2026-06-04) — old pin had `restartCount=0` across 17h of soak on the same pod spec; new pin is dying with `exit 137` (kubelet SIGKILL) every 3-4 min, no `OOMKilled: true` flag, no kernel OOM events.

### Symptom (from kubelet)

```
LAST SEEN  TYPE     REASON     OBJECT                            MESSAGE
9m18s      Warning  Unhealthy  pod/ai-central-7b99c5bb8c-nxglq   Startup probe failed: Get "http://10.0.3.81:18789/healthz": dial tcp 10.0.3.81:18789: connect: connection refused
```

Liveness probe is `httpGet :18789/healthz period=30s timeout=5s failure=3` (90s tolerance after startup).
Startup probe is `period=10s failure=18` (180s tolerance).

`status.containerStatuses[openclaw].lastState.terminated`:
```json
{"exitCode": 137, "reason": "Error", "startedAt": "14:49:33Z", "finishedAt": "14:53:06Z"}
```

3m33s lifetime, no `OOMKilled: true` flag → not a kernel OOM, this is kubelet's liveness-probe killer.

### Smoking-gun timeline from openclaw stdout

```
14:46:18.654  [gateway] loading configuration…
14:46:19.359  [gateway] starting...
14:46:31.072  [gateway] starting HTTP server...
14:46:31.083  [canvas] host mounted at http://0.0.0.0:18789/__openclaw__/canvas/
14:46:34.176  [gateway] agent model: google/gemini-2.5-flash
14:46:34.178  [gateway] http server listening (7 plugins: acpx, bonjour, browser,
                       device-pair, memory-core, phone-control, talk-voice; 14.8s)
14:46:39.066  [plugins] bonjour: watchdog detected non-announced service; attempting re-advertise
14:47:25.766  [plugins] bonjour: restarting advertiser (service stuck in probing for 46498ms)
14:48:35.288  [plugins] bonjour: watchdog detected non-announced service; attempting re-advertise
14:48:37.376  [plugins] embedded acpx runtime backend registered
14:48:39.254  [browser/server] Browser control listening on http://127.0.0.1:18791/
14:48:39.274  [gateway] ready                                  ← announces ready
14:48:39.280  [heartbeat] started
14:48:39.882  [openai-compat] chat completion failed: ...
14:48:41.872  [model-fallback/decision] decision=candidate_failed ... next=none
14:48:55.180  [plugins] document-extract staging bundled runtime deps
              (1 missing, 29 install specs): pdfjs-dist@^5.6.205             ← npm install AFTER ready
14:49:03.880  [plugins] document-extract installed bundled runtime deps in 8700ms
14:49:12.863  [plugins] microsoft staging bundled runtime deps
              (1 missing, 30 install specs): node-edge-tts@^1.2.10           ← npm install AFTER ready
14:49:18.261  [plugins] microsoft installed bundled runtime deps in 5398ms
14:49:32       [last line of stdout — container SIGKILLed]
```

So:
- `[gateway] ready` fires at 14:48:39
- Two heavy bundled-plugin npm installs (`pdfjs-dist`, `node-edge-tts`) run from 14:48:55 → 14:49:18 — ~23 seconds of single-threaded Node.js event-loop pressure
- Container is `cpu: 500m` (half a core hard limit) so npm install gets CPU-throttled and stretches in wall-clock
- `/healthz` polls run on the same event loop → three consecutive timeouts → kubelet SIGKILL at ~14:49:32

The old pin `20260521.4` either announced `ready` AFTER bundled-plugin deps were resolved, or did not have these bundled-plugin runtime-install paths at all. Either way, the contract `gateway ready ⇒ /healthz responsive` was honored.

### Why this matters

1. **The sidecar pattern guarantees in Kubernetes are about probe responsiveness**, not internal readiness. `[gateway] ready` is meaningless to kubelet — only `/healthz` returning 200 within timeout matters. The current behavior breaks that contract.

2. **`bonjour` already shows event-loop starvation symptoms** in the same window (`service stuck in probing for 46498ms` between 14:46:39 and 14:47:25 — 46s of starvation on a single watchdog). So plugin runtime work is provably blocking the loop for tens of seconds at a stretch even pre-ready, and post-ready does it again.

3. **Bundled plugin deps shouldn't install at runtime in the request-serving process at all.** They should land at image-build time (the canonical path), or in an init container, or in a worker process — anywhere except the same event loop that serves `/healthz`.

### Reproduction

Stand up openclaw `20260604.2` as a Kubernetes sidecar with:
- `cpu: 500m` / `memory: 1536Mi` limits
- Liveness probe `httpGet :18789/healthz period=30s timeout=5s failure=3`
- Any agent config that loads the `document-extract` and `microsoft` plugins (default profile in nail-notes-api ai-central does this)
- Cold pod start (no `/home/node/.openclaw/plugins/...` cache from a prior pod)

Container dies with exit 137 in ~3-4 min, repeating every restart cycle. Backing the same configmap with pin `20260521.4` does not reproduce.

### Suggested fixes (pick one or stack)

**(A) Don't announce `ready` until bundled plugin deps install completes.** Simplest, preserves the contract. Cost: ~25s longer to first-serve on cold cache.

**(B) Move bundled-plugin runtime-dep install to a build-time / image-time step.** Cleanest long-term. `pdfjs-dist` and `node-edge-tts` are not user-facing config — they're bundled-by-default deps and should be on disk before the container starts.

**(C) Move bundled-plugin runtime-dep install into a worker thread / subprocess.** Preserves cold-start latency but adds plumbing.

**(D) Bump `livenessProbe.timeoutSeconds` / `failureThreshold` in the consumer.** Workaround only — papering over a real event-loop-starvation issue and the bonjour starvation evidence suggests this can happen at any time (not just during plugin install).

## openclaw sidecar `20260604.2` killed by Kubernetes liveness probe after `gateway ready` due to runtime plugin-dep install starving event loop

**Repro context**: nail-notes-api `ai-central` deployment, openclaw running as a sidecar to a Go HTTP server. Pin bumped from `20260521.4` → `20260604.2` today (2026-06-04) — old pin had `restartCount=0` across 17h of soak on the same pod spec; new pin is dying with `exit 137` (kubelet SIGKILL) every 3-4 min, no `OOMKilled: true` flag, no kernel OOM events.

### Symptom (from kubelet)

```
LAST SEEN  TYPE     REASON     OBJECT                            MESSAGE
9m18s      Warning  Unhealthy  pod/ai-central-7b99c5bb8c-nxglq   Startup probe failed: Get "http://10.0.3.81:18789/healthz": dial tcp 10.0.3.81:18789: connect: connection refused
```

Liveness probe is `httpGet :18789/healthz period=30s timeout=5s failure=3` (90s tolerance after startup).
Startup probe is `period=10s failure=18` (180s tolerance).

`status.containerStatuses[openclaw].lastState.terminated`:
```json
{"exitCode": 137, "reason": "Error", "startedAt": "14:49:33Z", "finishedAt": "14:53:06Z"}
```

3m33s lifetime, no `OOMKilled: true` flag → not a kernel OOM, this is kubelet's liveness-probe killer.

### Smoking-gun timeline from openclaw stdout

```
14:46:18.654  [gateway] loading configuration…
14:46:19.359  [gateway] starting...
14:46:31.072  [gateway] starting HTTP server...
14:46:31.083  [canvas] host mounted at http://0.0.0.0:18789/__openclaw__/canvas/
14:46:34.176  [gateway] agent model: google/gemini-2.5-flash
14:46:34.178  [gateway] http server listening (7 plugins: acpx, bonjour, browser,
                       device-pair, memory-core, phone-control, talk-voice; 14.8s)
14:46:39.066  [plugins] bonjour: watchdog detected non-announced service; attempting re-advertise
14:47:25.766  [plugins] bonjour: restarting advertiser (service stuck in probing for 46498ms)
14:48:35.288  [plugins] bonjour: watchdog detected non-announced service; attempting re-advertise
14:48:37.376  [plugins] embedded acpx runtime backend registered
14:48:39.254  [browser/server] Browser control listening on http://127.0.0.1:18791/
14:48:39.274  [gateway] ready                                  ← announces ready
14:48:39.280  [heartbeat] started
14:48:39.882  [openai-compat] chat completion failed: ...
14:48:41.872  [model-fallback/decision] decision=candidate_failed ... next=none
14:48:55.180  [plugins] document-extract staging bundled runtime deps
              (1 missing, 29 install specs): pdfjs-dist@^5.6.205             ← npm install AFTER ready
14:49:03.880  [plugins] document-extract installed bundled runtime deps in 8700ms
14:49:12.863  [plugins] microsoft staging bundled runtime deps
              (1 missing, 30 install specs): node-edge-tts@^1.2.10           ← npm install AFTER ready
14:49:18.261  [plugins] microsoft installed bundled runtime deps in 5398ms
14:49:32       [last line of stdout — container SIGKILLed]
```

So:
- `[gateway] ready` fires at 14:48:39
- Two heavy bundled-plugin npm installs (`pdfjs-dist`, `node-edge-tts`) run from 14:48:55 → 14:49:18 — ~23 seconds of single-threaded Node.js event-loop pressure
- Container is `cpu: 500m` (half a core hard limit) so npm install gets CPU-throttled and stretches in wall-clock
- `/healthz` polls run on the same event loop → three consecutive timeouts → kubelet SIGKILL at ~14:49:32

The old pin `20260521.4` either announced `ready` AFTER bundled-plugin deps were resolved, or did not have these bundled-plugin runtime-install paths at all. Either way, the contract `gateway ready ⇒ /healthz responsive` was honored.

### Why this matters

1. **The sidecar pattern guarantees in Kubernetes are about probe responsiveness**, not internal readiness. `[gateway] ready` is meaningless to kubelet — only `/healthz` returning 200 within timeout matters. The current behavior breaks that contract.

2. **`bonjour` already shows event-loop starvation symptoms** in the same window (`service stuck in probing for 46498ms` between 14:46:39 and 14:47:25 — 46s of starvation on a single watchdog). So plugin runtime work is provably blocking the loop for tens of seconds at a stretch even pre-ready, and post-ready does it again.

3. **Bundled plugin deps shouldn't install at runtime in the request-serving process at all.** They should land at image-build time (the canonical path), or in an init container, or in a worker process — anywhere except the same event loop that serves `/healthz`.

### Reproduction

Stand up openclaw `20260604.2` as a Kubernetes sidecar with:
- `cpu: 500m` / `memory: 1536Mi` limits
- Liveness probe `httpGet :18789/healthz period=30s timeout=5s failure=3`
- Any agent config that loads the `document-extract` and `microsoft` plugins (default profile in nail-notes-api ai-central does this)
- Cold pod start (no `/home/node/.openclaw/plugins/...` cache from a prior pod)

Container dies with exit 137 in ~3-4 min, repeating every restart cycle. Backing the same configmap with pin `20260521.4` does not reproduce.

### Suggested fixes (pick one or stack)

**(A) Don't announce `ready` until bundled plugin deps install completes.** Simplest, preserves the contract. Cost: ~25s longer to first-serve on cold cache.

**(B) Move bundled-plugin runtime-dep install to a build-time / image-time step.** Cleanest long-term. `pdfjs-dist` and `node-edge-tts` are not user-facing config — they're bundled-by-default deps and should be on disk before the container starts.

**(C) Move bundled-plugin runtime-dep install into a worker thread / subprocess.** Preserves cold-start latency but adds plumbing.

**(D) Bump `livenessProbe.timeoutSeconds` / `failureThreshold` in the consumer.** Workaround only — papering over a real event-loop-starvation issue and the bonjour starvation evidence suggests this can happen at any time (not just during plugin install).

We're going to apply (D) as an emergency workaround on the ai-central deployment to get test cluster recovering today, but the openclaw-side fix should be (A) or (B). Happy to test patches against ai-central if a release candidate is cut.

### Related on consumer side

- nail-notes-api GH-5778 (https://github.com/smisy/nail-notes-api/issues/5778) — full diagnostic chain
- nail-notes-api GH-5768 — the pin bump that surfaced this

### Affected versions

- Bad: `nailnotesserviceacr.azurecr.io/openclaw:20260604.2` (upstream `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.4.26` base)
- Good: `nailnotesserviceacr.azurecr.io/openclaw:20260521.4`

Per the GH-5768 verification trail, the only changes between `20260521.4` and `20260604.2` in the upstream openclaw repo were GH-5562 (graphql-proxy nail-service routing) and GH-5585 (unrelated) — neither obviously touches plugin runtime-install or gateway-ready ordering. So the regression may actually be in a transitive bundled-plugin dep version bump that triggered the missing-runtime-dep `install_specs` path. Worth a `git log` on the document-extract and microsoft plugin manifests between the two tag dates.

cc @nails-cloud-system-design (consumer side / can repro + verify patches)

question_text:

The mirror append changes the same `.jsonl` file, so the embedded runner can treat OpenClaw's own internal delivery mirror write as an external session takeover and abort with:

answer_text:

thread_text:
ISSUE #90307: message_tool_only delivery-mirror can trip EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError by writing outside the active embedded session writer
Author: wangzitian0
Date: 2026-06-04T11:43:49Z
Labels: P1, impact:session-state, impact:message-loss
State: closed

[c0]
## Summary

In `message_tool_only` source reply mode, a successful `message(action="send")` can append a `provider=openclaw`, `model=delivery-mirror` assistant entry to the same active session transcript via a standalone transcript append path. During an embedded run, the prompt lock has been released and the session file fingerprint fence is active. The mirror append changes the same `.jsonl` file, so the embedded runner can treat OpenClaw's own internal delivery mirror write as an external session takeover and abort with:

```text
EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError: session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released: <sessionFile>
```

This is a narrower source-level shape for the broader session takeover class reported in related issues.

## Environment observed

- OpenClaw: `2026.5.18`
- Runtime: Docker gateway
- Channel: Discord group/channel session
- Source reply mode: `messages.groupChat.visibleReplies = "message_tool"`
- Agent model: `openai-codex/gpt-5.5`

## Minimal reproduction shape

This should not require a real Discord setup; Discord is just where I observed it. The minimum ingredients are:

1. Run an embedded agent turn for a persisted session key.
2. Use source reply mode `message_tool_only` (for example, group/channel visible replies configured as `message_tool`).
3. Make the agent send the visible reply through:

```text
message(action="send", message="pong")
```

4. The message delivery path appends a `delivery-mirror` assistant message to the current session transcript.
5. The active embedded run later reacquires the session write lock and checks the fingerprint fence.

Expected: the run completes normally because the mirror write is OpenClaw-internal bookkeeping for the same turn.

Actual: the run can abort with `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` because the same session file changed while the prompt lock was released.

## Live transcript shape observed

The affected session transcript had only this small shape around the turn:

```jsonl
{"type":"message","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"... ping 0604"}]}}
{"type":"custom_message","customType":"openclaw.runtime-context", ...}
{"type":"message","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"toolCall","name":"message","arguments":{"action":"send","message":"pong 0604"}}],"provider":"openai-codex","model":"gpt-5.5","stopReason":"toolUse"}}
{"type":"message","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"pong 0604"}],"provider":"openclaw","model":"delivery-mirror","stopReason":"stop"}}
```

Shortly after that mirror entry, the gateway logged paired lane errors for the same session file:

```text
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main ... EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError: session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released: <sessionFile>
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=session:agent:<agent>:discord:channel:<channel> ... EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError: session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released: <sessionFile>
Embedded agent failed before reply: session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released: <sessionFile>
```

I did not find evidence of multiple gateway processes, multiple agents writing this session, or a plugin writing this `agents/<agent>/sessions/*.jsonl` file. The observed write that changed the file was the `delivery-mirror` entry itself.

## Why this looks like an internal writer boundary issue

The expected invariant is effectively one active writer per session file / session key. In this case the invariant is broken by two OpenClaw-internal write paths for the same active turn:

- the active embedded run's session manager writes normal user/assistant/tool transcript entries;
- the `message_tool_only` source reply mirror writes the `delivery-mirror` entry through a standalone transcript append path.

That second path appears to bypass the active embedded attempt's session writer / fence refresh boundary, so the fence cannot distinguish an internal mirror write from an external takeover.

## Suggested minimal fix direction

For `message_tool_only` source reply mirror writes targeting the currently active embedded session:

1. Prefer appending the `delivery-mirror` through the active session manager / active embedded session writer, so existing session guards, hooks, transcript caches, and fence refresh all see it as part of the same run; or
2. Pass an explicit current-run/session-write context to the mirror append path and mark that write as an owned internal write for the current lock controller.

The standalone `appendAssistantMessageToSessionTranscript` path should still exist for cases where there is no active session writer, such as recovery, proactive delivery, or cross-session persistence.

Things that would be risky as a fix:

- swallowing `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` globally;
- removing `delivery-mirror` transcript persistence;
- changing all `message_tool_only` rooms back to automatic visible replies;
- adding a global agent lock instead of keeping the session-key boundary.

## Regression tests that would prove the fix

1. `message_tool_only` embedded run + `message(action="send")` writes one `delivery-mirror` entry and does not throw `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError`.
2. The same test verifies the mirror remains transcript-only (`provider=openclaw`, `model=delivery-mirror`) and is not delivered twice.
3. Ordinary automatic visible replies still work unchanged.
4. Standalone/cross-session mirror append still works when no active session writer exists.
5. A real external append to the same session while the prompt lock is released should still trip the takeover guard.

## Related issues

This appears related to, but narrower than, the existing takeover reports:

- #86508 - Discord runs failing with `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError`.
- #86966 - paired lanes on the same session racing after prompt-lock release.
- #84059 - Feishu runs failing with the same fence error on 2026.5.18.
- #88703 - yielded/image generation path where legitimate announce-run writes were not visible to the original lock controller.
- #89734 - silent user-visible failure when takeover terminates a run.

It also touches the delivery-mirror / transcript-mirroring family:

- #87994 - delivery-mirror duplicate delivery symptoms.
- #85669 - delivery-mirror entries leaking into session history/dashboard.
- #73274 - plugin/API discussion around direct transcript append.
- #88757 / #74743 - proactive or scheduled messages delivered to channels but not consistently represented in session context.
- #69208 - umbrella for duplicate transcript/replay/context issues.

comments.body:
## Summary

In `message_tool_only` source reply mode, a successful `message(action="send")` can append a `provider=openclaw`, `model=delivery-mirror` assistant entry to the same active session transcript via a standalone transcript append path. During an embedded run, the prompt lock has been released and the session file fingerprint fence is active. The mirror append changes the same `.jsonl` file, so the embedded runner can treat OpenClaw's own internal delivery mirror write as an external session takeover and abort with:

```text
EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError: session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released: <sessionFile>
```

This is a narrower source-level shape for the broader session takeover class reported in related issues.

## Environment observed

- OpenClaw: `2026.5.18`
- Runtime: Docker gateway
- Channel: Discord group/channel session
- Source reply mode: `messages.groupChat.visibleReplies = "message_tool"`
- Agent model: `openai-codex/gpt-5.5`

## Minimal reproduction shape

This should not require a real Discord setup; Discord is just where I observed it. The minimum ingredients are:

1. Run an embedded agent turn for a persisted session key.
2. Use source reply mode `message_tool_only` (for example, group/channel visible replies configured as `message_tool`).
3. Make the agent send the visible reply through:

```text
message(action="send", message="pong")
```

4. The message delivery path appends a `delivery-mirror` assistant message to the current session transcript.
5. The active embedded run later reacquires the session write lock and checks the fingerprint fence.

Expected: the run completes normally because the mirror write is OpenClaw-internal bookkeeping for the same turn.

Actual: the run can abort with `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` because the same session file changed while the prompt lock was released.

## Live transcript shape observed

The affected session transcript had only this small shape around the turn:

```jsonl
{"type":"message","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"... ping 0604"}]}}
{"type":"custom_message","customType":"openclaw.runtime-context", ...}
{"type":"message","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"toolCall","name":"message","arguments":{"action":"send","message":"pong 0604"}}],"provider":"openai-codex","model":"gpt-5.5","stopReason":"toolUse"}}
{"type":"message","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"pong 0604"}],"provider":"openclaw","model":"delivery-mirror","stopReason":"stop"}}
```

Shortly after that mirror entry, the gateway logged paired lane errors for the same session file:

```text
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main ... EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError: session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released: <sessionFile>
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=session:agent:<agent>:discord:channel:<channel> ... EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError: session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released: <sessionFile>
Embedded agent failed before reply: session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released: <sessionFile>
```

I did not find evidence of multiple gateway processes, multiple agents writing this session, or a plugin writing this `agents/<agent>/sessions/*.jsonl` file. The observed write that changed the file was the `delivery-mirror` entry itself.

## Why this looks like an internal writer boundary issue

The expected invariant is effectively one active writer per session file / session key. In this case the invariant is broken by two OpenClaw-internal write paths for the same active turn:

- the active embedded run's session manager writes normal user/assistant/tool transcript entries;
- the `message_tool_only` source reply mirror writes the `delivery-mirror` entry through a standalone transcript append path.

That second path appears to bypass the active embedded attempt's session writer / fence refresh boundary, so the fence cannot distinguish an internal mirror write from an external takeover.

## Suggested minimal fix direction

For `message_tool_only` source reply mirror writes targeting the currently active embedded session:

1. Prefer appending the `delivery-mirror` through the active session manager / active embedded session writer, so existing session guards, hooks, transcript caches, and fence refresh all see it as part of the same run; or
2. Pass an explicit current-run/session-write context to the mirror append path and mark that write as an owned internal write for the current lock controller.

The standalone `appendAssistantMessageToSessionTranscript` path should still exist for cases where there is no active session writer, such as recovery, proactive delivery, or cross-session persistence.

Things that would be risky as a fix:

- swallowing `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` globally;
- removing `delivery-mirror` transcript persistence;
- changing all `message_tool_only` rooms back to automatic visible replies;
- adding a global agent lock instead of keeping the session-key boundary.

## Regression tests that would prove the fix

1. `message_tool_only` embedded run + `message(action="send")` writes one `delivery-mirror` entry and does not throw `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError`.
2. The same test verifies the mirror remains transcript-only (`provider=openclaw`, `model=delivery-mirror`) and is not delivered twice.
3. Ordinary automatic visible replies still work unchanged.
4. Standalone/cross-session mirror append still works when no active session writer exists.
5. A real external append to the same session while the prompt lock is released should still trip the takeover guard.

## Related issues

This appears related to, but narrower than, the existing takeover reports:

- #86508 - Discord runs failing with `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError`.
- #86966 - paired lanes on the same session racing after prompt-lock release.
- #84059 - Feishu runs failing with the same fence error on 2026.5.18.
- #88703 - yielded/image generation path where legitimate announce-run writes were not visible to the original lock controller.
- #89734 - silent user-visible failure when takeover terminates a run.

It also touches the delivery-mirror / transcript-mirroring family:

- #87994 - delivery-mirror duplicate delivery symptoms.
- #85669 - delivery-mirror entries leaking into session history/dashboard.
- #73274 - plugin/API discussion around direct transcript append.
- #88757 / #74743 - proactive or scheduled messages delivered to channels but not consistently represented in session context.
- #69208 - umbrella for duplicate transcript/replay/context issues.

# Codex/ChatGPT OAuth: `400 (no body)` on `openai-chatgpt-responses` after upgrade to 2026.6.1 (Windows)

## Summary
After upgrading from `2026.5.28` to `2026.6.1`, agents using the ChatGPT/Codex OAuth subscription (GPT-5.5 via `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex`) stop working. Every request returns `400 (no body)` and the agent silently falls back to its configured fallback model. Rolling back to `2026.5.28` fully restores Codex routing with the same OAuth login.

## Environment
- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200, x64)
- Node: 24.14.0
- OpenClaw: 2026.6.1 (broken) vs 2026.5.28 (works)
- Provider: ChatGPT subscription OAuth (Codex), model `gpt-5.5`
- Auth: valid OAuth login (`codex login status` => "Logged in using ChatGPT"), token refreshed same day, quota healthy (`models status` shows `openai usage: 5h 98% left`)

## What happens on 2026.6.1
1. `openclaw config validate` on the pre-upgrade config fails with:
   ```
   models.providers.<codex-provider>.models.*.api: Invalid input
   (allowed: ... "openai-chatgpt-responses" ...)
   <codex-provider> is legacy; run "openclaw doctor --fix"
   ```
   The previously-valid api value `openai-codex-responses` is no longer accepted.
2. `openclaw doctor --fix` migrates the legacy Codex provider, renames the OAuth auth profile, and rewrites agent model strings.
3. After migration, every Codex call fails:
   ```
   [responses] error provider=<codex> api=openai-chatgpt-responses model=gpt-5.5
   name=Error status=400 code=undefined type=undefined message=400 status code (no body)
   ```
   The agent then falls back to its fallback model.

## What I verified
- OAuth login is valid and freshly refreshed (token good for ~8 more days).
- `models status` reports the ChatGPT/Codex quota under the `openai` provider as healthy (`5h 98% left`).
- The new build hardcodes the Codex base URL for `openai-chatgpt-responses` (so a per-provider baseUrl override does not change the target).
- `OPENAI_AUTH_PROVIDER_IDS` is `["openai"]` in 2026.6.1, and `hasAvailableCodexAuth` requires an OAuth/token profile under provider id `openai`. I wired the config to match (provider `openai`, api `openai-chatgpt-responses`, oauth profile under `openai:`), and the request still returns `400 (no body)`.
- Same machine, same OAuth credential, `2026.5.28` works immediately after rollback.

## Expected
`gpt-5.5` over the ChatGPT/Codex OAuth subscription should continue to work after upgrading to 2026.6.1, or `doctor --fix` should produce a config that actually round-trips against the Codex backend.

## Actual
All Codex requests return `400 (no body)`; agents silently fall back.

## Workaround
Roll back to `2026.5.28` and restore the pre-migration config (which keeps the legacy Codex provider + `openai-codex-responses` api). Codex routing then works.

## Questions for maintainers
1. What is the exact required request shape / api id for ChatGPT-subscription Codex OAuth in 2026.6.1?
2. Is `400 (no body)` from `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex` a known transport regression in 2026.6.1?
3. Does `doctor --fix` fully migrate ChatGPT-OAuth Codex setups, or is manual config required post-upgrade?

thread_text:
ISSUE #90190: [Bug]: Codex native tool-progress lines leak into WhatsApp as standalone messages (Telegram-only fix #71351 doesn't cover WhatsApp)
Author: 2vanm
Date: 2026-06-04T06:02:58Z
Labels: P2, impact:message-loss
State: closed

[c0]

### Summary

On WhatsApp, Codex native Code Mode tool-progress status lines are delivered to the user as **standalone messages** during tool-heavy turns, e.g.:

```
🛠️ `print lines 1-220 from memory/2026-06-03.md (agent)`
🛠️ `jq -c 'select(.id == "act-…")' brain/actions-taken.jsonl (agent)`
🛠️ `print text (agent)`
🩹 Apply Patch
```

This is the same class of bug as #71320 (Telegram), which was fixed by #71351 — but that fix was explicitly **Telegram-scoped**, and WhatsApp has no equivalent fix and **no config lever** to disable it.

### Version

- OpenClaw `2026.5.22`
- Agent runtime: `openai-codex` (gpt-5.5), Codex native Code Mode
- Channel: WhatsApp (Baileys), DM

### Onset

First-ever occurrence in a ~20k-line outbound audit log is **3 days after upgrading 2026.5.12 → 2026.5.22**. Zero occurrences in all prior (≤5.12) history; recurs on every sufficiently tool-heavy turn since. The 2026.5.18 release notes mention reworked "native tool progress" + Codex code-mode, which lines up.

### Root cause (from reading the installed bundle)

- The native-tool-progress *draft* path (`canUseNativeToolProgressDraftForChat`, `bot-*.js`) is gated on `telegramCfg` — it only applies to Telegram. WhatsApp can't edit a draft message in place, so when the agent emits tool-progress items there is no preview/draft to collapse them into, and each becomes its own outbound payload via `deliverOutboundPayloads`.
- `#71351` set `resolveChannelStreamingPreviewToolProgress()` default `false` and `suppressDefaultToolProgressMessages: true` **for Telegram only** (`extensions/telegram/…`). The PR states: *"The change is Telegram-scoped."*
- `resolveChannelStreamingSuppressDefaultToolProgressMessages(entry, …)` returns `false` when preview-stream `mode === "off"`, and otherwise only suppresses when a **draft stream is active** — which never happens on WhatsApp.
- The strict WhatsApp config schema (`WhatsAppConfigSchema` = `.strict()` in `bundled-channel-config-schema-*.js`) has **no `streaming` / `preview` / `nativeToolProgress` / `toolProgress` key** — those exist only on the Telegram/Discord/Slack/Matrix/Teams schemas. So there is no `channels.whatsapp.*` setting that can suppress this. (`blockStreaming: true` is accepted and set, and does **not** stop it — the leaks predate and survive it.)
- The "add an option to suppress tool-call progress messages per channel" request (#19025), which explicitly names WhatsApp, was closed as *not planned*.

Net: every Codex + WhatsApp user gets these internal status lines as chat spam, with no supported way to turn them off.

### Expected

Native tool-progress status lines should never be delivered as standalone messages on a channel that has no editable preview/draft surface (WhatsApp, and likely SMS/other Baileys-style channels). Either:

1. Extend the #71351 suppression so non-draft channels default to **not** emitting standalone native tool-progress messages; or
2. Expose a channel-generic / per-channel `toolProgress: "off"` lever (reviving #19025) that the strict WhatsApp schema accepts.

### Actual

Standalone `🛠️ … (agent)` / `🩹 Apply Patch` messages on every tool-heavy WhatsApp turn.

### Current workaround (for others hitting this)

Because there is no config lever, the only working mitigation is a **plugin** registering a `message_sending` hook (the per-payload modifying hook in `deliverOutboundPayloads` / `applyMessageSendingHook`) that returns `{ cancel: true }` for lines that start with a tool emoji and end with the `(agent)` source label, or start with `🩹`. A *workspace* hook does **not** work: workspace hooks register as internal hooks (`registerInternalHook`), which are observe-only (`triggerInternalHook` discards the return), and there is no internal `message:sending` event — the cancellable seam is the plugin-SDK `message_sending` hook only.

title: Prompt injection: external content in web_fetch _meta field bypasses EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT wrapper
need_summary: Whether the reported prompt-injection bypass in web_fetch’s _meta field was already fixed by the current wrapping/whitelisting behavior documented in `src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts` and release commit `2e08f0f4221f` (v2026.6.1).
security_topic: trust-boundary bypass in web_fetch tool output
question_text:
## Summary

External page content fetched via web_fetch can be injected into the _meta field of the tool result without the EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT wrapper or security notice that protects the main text/markdown payload. A crafted page can embed a tool_call block in this unwrapped field, attempting to get the agent to execute a follow-up tool call.
answer_text:
Thanks for the context here. I did a careful shell check against current `main`, and this is already implemented.

Current main and the shipped v2026.6.1 tag already close the reported trust-boundary gap: web_fetch model-visible text is wrapped, provider fallback fields are normalized through a whitelist, and transcript-only toolResult.details are stripped before provider conversion.

So I’m closing this as already implemented rather than keeping a duplicate issue open.
thread_text:
ISSUE #90402: Prompt injection: external content in web_fetch _meta field bypasses EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT wrapper
Author: Udjin79
Date: 2026-06-04T15:51:23Z
Labels: P2, impact:security
State: closed

[c0]
## Summary

External page content fetched via web_fetch can be injected into the _meta field of the tool result without the EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT wrapper or security notice that protects the main text/markdown payload. A crafted page can embed a tool_call block in this unwrapped field, attempting to get the agent to execute a follow-up tool call.

## What happened

While fetching a JS-rendered page (the main body came back nearly empty), the tool result contained an _meta entry whose content field held external page text with an embedded tool_call block requesting a follow-up web_fetch. The embedded block is external page content masquerading as a legitimate agent-issued tool call.

## Root cause

The main text/markdown payload from web_fetch is correctly wrapped in a SECURITY NOTICE plus EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT block. But the _meta.*.content field carries external page content without any wrapper or untrusted marker. One field of the same tool result is sanitized; another is not. Inconsistent trust boundary.

## Impact

- Prompt-injection vector that bypasses the existing untrusted-content guard.
- Any external fetch that populates _meta can attempt to drive agent tool calls via this unwrapped channel.
- The purpose of the EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT wrapper is defeated if a parallel field skips it.

## Expected behavior

Any field in a tool result that can contain external/untrusted content should get the same treatment as the main payload: wrapped in EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT with the security notice, or stripped of model-actionable structures (e.g. tool_call blocks) before being surfaced to the model.

## Notes

- The injection was ignored by the agent; no unintended tool call was executed.
- Reported from a real session (web_fetch on a JS-rendered page; beta v2026.6.x build train).


--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @clawsweeper 2026-06-04T15:53:04Z:
Thanks for the context here. I did a careful shell check against current `main`, and this is already implemented.

Current main and the shipped v2026.6.1 tag already close the reported trust-boundary gap: web_fetch model-visible text is wrapped, provider fallback fields are normalized through a whitelist, and transcript-only toolResult.details are stripped before provider conversion.

So I’m closing this as already implemented rather than keeping a duplicate issue open.

<details>
<summary>Review details</summary>

Best possible solution:

Keep the shipped web_fetch wrapping, provider-payload whitelisting, and LLM-boundary details stripping in place; broader prompt-injection architecture can continue in the existing security design discussions.

Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue?

No high-confidence current-main reproduction remains. Source inspection shows web_fetch content fields are wrapped or discarded, and toolResult.details are removed before provider conversion.

Is this the best way to solve the issue?

Yes. The current fix is at the right boundary: normalize web_fetch provider output before returning it and strip transcript-only details before anything crosses the LLM provider boundary.

Security review:

Security review cleared: Current main and v2026.6.1 already wrap or remove the reported untrusted web_fetch side-channel content before it reaches model input.

AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant.

What I checked:

- **Current web_fetch wrapping:** Current main wraps web_fetch text with wrapWebContent/wrapExternalContent and wraps title/warning fields through wrapWebFetchField. ([`src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts:215`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3e6978770a82/src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts#L215), [3e6978770a82](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3e6978770a82))
- **Provider payload whitelist:** Provider fallback payloads are rebuilt from known fields; arbitrary provider keys such as _meta are not copied into the returned web_fetch payload, while text/title/warning are wrapped. ([`src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts:335`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3e6978770a82/src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts#L335), [3e6978770a82](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3e6978770a82))

([`src/agents/tools/web-fetch.provider-fallback.test.ts:40`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3e6978770a82/src/agents/tools/web-fetch.provider-fallback.test.ts#L40), [3e6978770a82](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3e6978770a82))
- **Git history provenance:** Blame attributes the current web_fetch wrapping and tool-result details stripping paths in this shallow checkout to commit 1ce11fbf423b2c0fc7be76504af420de447136aa; the current source carries that behavior forward. ([`src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts:215`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1ce11fbf423b/src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts#L215), [1ce11fbf423b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1ce11fbf423b))
- **Release provenance:** The v2026.6.1 release commit contains the same web_fetch wrapping and field normalization behavior; diffing v2026.6.1 to current main on the relevant files shows only comment additions for these paths. ([`src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts:215`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2e08f0f4221f/src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts#L215), [2e08f0f4221f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2e08f0f4221f))

Likely related people:

- **Peter Steinberger:** Blame and path history in this checkout attribute the web_fetch wrapping, provider fallback normalization, and tool-result details stripping code to commits by Peter Steinberger. (role: recent area contributor; confidence: high; commits: [1ce11fbf423b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1ce11fbf423b2c0fc7be76504af420de447136aa), [041fab7b7275](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/041fab7b72754847a641c3a464c5111641f6e424); files: `src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts`, `src/agents/session-transcript-repair.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.llm-boundary.ts`)

(role: release provenance; confidence: medium; commits: [2e08f0f4221f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2e08f0f4221f522b60423ed6ffd83427942b28de); files: `src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts`, `src/agents/session-transcript-repair.ts`)

ISSUE #90392: Feature: per-agent MCP server scoping in mcp.servers for non-Codex sessions
Author: podulator
Date: 2026-06-04T15:29:01Z
Labels: P2, impact:security, impact:other
State: closed

[c0]
## Summary

`mcp.servers` entries are currently offered to all agents at session start, regardless of which agents actually need them. The only way to restrict access is via `tools.allow`/`tools.deny` policy, which strips tools *after* they've already been offered — generating noisy `tool policy removed N tool(s)` log entries on every session spawn for every agent that doesn't need those tools.

## Current behaviour

Given a config like:
```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "yfinance-price-tracker": { "transport": "sse", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8767/sse" }
    }
  },
  "agents": {
    "list": [
      { "id": "analena", "tools": { "allow": ["yfinance-price-tracker__*", ...] } },
      { "id": "harvey",  "tools": { "allow": ["read", "write", ...] } }
    ]
  }
}
```

The gateway offers all 17 yfinance tools to **every** agent at session start, then strips them via `tools.allow` policy for the 6 agents that don't need them. Each strip generates a log entry. On a 7-agent setup with a 30-minute heartbeat cron per agent, this produces ~100+ redundant strip events per day.

## What was tried

`mcp.servers.*.codex.agents` — accepted by config validation but has no effect on regular OpenClaw sessions (Codex app-server projection only, as documented).

Per-agent `mcp` block in `agents.list` — rejected by schema validation (`agents.list.6: Invalid input`).

`toolFilter.exclude: ["*"]` — server-level filter, applies to all agents equally, can't be used to scope to a subset.

## Requested behaviour

A way to declare that an MCP server should only be offered to specific agent IDs *before* tool policy filtering. Something like:

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "yfinance-price-tracker": {
        "transport": "sse",
        "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8767/sse",
        "agents": ["analena"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The `codex.agents` concept already exists for Codex app-server projection — this is the same idea extended to the main session tool inventory path.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.5.28
- 7 agents, 1 SSE MCP server scoped to 1 agent via `tools.allow`
- Raspberry Pi arm64, `openclaw-gateway.service` systemd user service

ISSUE #90391: [Feature]: Support Custom Sandbox Backends
Author: sjy3
Date: 2026-06-04T15:27:31Z
Labels: enhancement, P3, impact:security
State: closed

[c0]
### Summary

Would OpenClaw consider adding a pluggable sandbox backend abstraction so Docker remains the default, while remote sandbox runtimes can integrate with the existing sandbox tool surface?

### Problem to solve

Without a pluggable sandbox backend, remote sandbox providers usually need to expose separate plugin tools such as `remote_sandbox_exec`, `remote_sandbox_read`, or `remote_sandbox_write`.

This does not preserve the existing OpenClaw sandbox experience across:

- `exec`
- `process`
- file read/write
- `edit`
- `apply_patch`
- sandbox lifecycle commands


### Proposed solution

Introduce a sandbox backend abstraction that keeps the current Docker behavior unchanged, while allowing future backends to be added.

A minimal first step could be:

1. Add an internal `SandboxBackend` interface.
2. Move the current Docker implementation behind `DockerSandboxBackend`.
3. Add a config option such as `sandbox.backend`, defaulting to `docker`.
4. Ensure unsupported or unavailable backends fail closed instead of falling back to host execution.
5. Consider exposing backend registration to plugins after the internal interface stabilizes.


Expected Benefits

- Support remote sandbox runtimes without replacing built-in tools.
- Preserve existing sandbox semantics such as `mode`, `scope`, and `workspaceAccess`.
- Improve production deployment flexibility.
- Keep sandbox boundaries explicit and auditable.
- Avoid teaching the model to use separate remote-specific tools.

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Impact

This proposal only adds a `SandboxBackend` interface abstraction and backend registration mechanism on top of the current sandbox design.

Expected impact:

- Existing sandbox backends and Docker behavior remain unchanged.
- Current sandbox configuration and tool behavior remain compatible.
- New custom sandbox backends can be registered through the new abstraction.
- Existing users do not need to change their setup.
- The implementation should be incremental and low-risk, since it does not replace or remove any current sandbox backend.

### Evidence/examples

### Summary

Would OpenClaw consider adding a pluggable sandbox backend abstraction so Docker remains the default, while remote sandbox runtimes can integrate with the existing sandbox tool surface?

### Problem to solve

Without a pluggable sandbox backend, remote sandbox providers usually need to expose separate plugin tools such as `remote_sandbox_exec`, `remote_sandbox_read`, or `remote_sandbox_write`.

This does not preserve the existing OpenClaw sandbox experience across:

- `exec`
- `process`
- file read/write
- `edit`
- `apply_patch`
- sandbox lifecycle commands


### Proposed solution

Introduce a sandbox backend abstraction that keeps the current Docker behavior unchanged, while allowing future backends to be added.

A minimal first step could be:

1. Add an internal `SandboxBackend` interface.
2. Move the current Docker implementation behind `DockerSandboxBackend`.
3. Add a config option such as `sandbox.backend`, defaulting to `docker`.
4. Ensure unsupported or unavailable backends fail closed instead of falling back to host execution.
5. Consider exposing backend registration to plugins after the internal interface stabilizes.


Expected Benefits

- Support remote sandbox runtimes without replacing built-in tools.
- Preserve existing sandbox semantics such as `mode`, `scope`, and `workspaceAccess`.
- Improve production deployment flexibility.
- Keep sandbox boundaries explicit and auditable.
- Avoid teaching the model to use separate remote-specific tools.

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Impact

This proposal only adds a `SandboxBackend` interface abstraction and backend registration mechanism on top of the current sandbox design.

Expected impact:

- Existing sandbox backends and Docker behavior remain unchanged.
- Current sandbox configuration and tool behavior remain compatible.
- New custom sandbox backends can be registered through the new abstraction.
- Existing users do not need to change their setup.
- The implementation should be incremental and low-risk, since it does not replace or remove any current sandbox backend.

## openclaw sidecar `20260604.2` killed by Kubernetes liveness probe after `gateway ready` due to runtime plugin-dep install starving event loop

**Repro context**: nail-notes-api `ai-central` deployment, openclaw running as a sidecar to a Go HTTP server. Pin bumped from `20260521.4` → `20260604.2` today (2026-06-04) — old pin had `restartCount=0` across 17h of soak on the same pod spec; new pin is dying with `exit 137` (kubelet SIGKILL) every 3-4 min, no `OOMKilled: true` flag, no kernel OOM events.

### Symptom (from kubelet)

```
LAST SEEN  TYPE     REASON     OBJECT                            MESSAGE
9m18s      Warning  Unhealthy  pod/ai-central-7b99c5bb8c-nxglq   Startup probe failed: Get "http://10.0.3.81:18789/healthz": dial tcp 10.0.3.81:18789: connect: connection refused
```

Liveness probe is `httpGet :18789/healthz period=30s timeout=5s failure=3` (90s tolerance after startup).
Startup probe is `period=10s failure=18` (180s tolerance).

`status.containerStatuses[openclaw].lastState.terminated`:
```json
{"exitCode": 137, "reason": "Error", "startedAt": "14:49:33Z", "finishedAt": "14:53:06Z"}
```

3m33s lifetime, no `OOMKilled: true` flag → not a kernel OOM, this is kubelet's liveness-probe killer.

### Smoking-gun timeline from openclaw stdout

```
14:46:18.654  [gateway] loading configuration…
14:46:19.359  [gateway] starting...
14:46:31.072  [gateway] starting HTTP server...
14:46:31.083  [canvas] host mounted at http://0.0.0.0:18789/__openclaw__/canvas/
14:46:34.176  [gateway] agent model: google/gemini-2.5-flash
14:46:34.178  [gateway] http server listening (7 plugins: acpx, bonjour, browser,
                       device-pair, memory-core, phone-control, talk-voice; 14.8s)
14:46:39.066  [plugins] bonjour: watchdog detected non-announced service; attempting re-advertise
14:47:25.766  [plugins] bonjour: restarting advertiser (service stuck in probing for 46498ms)
14:48:35.288  [plugins] bonjour: watchdog detected non-announced service; attempting re-advertise
14:48:37.376  [plugins] embedded acpx runtime backend registered
14:48:39.254  [browser/server] Browser control listening on http://127.0.0.1:18791/
14:48:39.274  [gateway] ready                                  ← announces ready
14:48:39.280  [heartbeat] started
14:48:39.882  [openai-compat] chat completion failed: ...
14:48:41.872  [model-fallback/decision] decision=candidate_failed ... next=none
14:48:55.180  [plugins] document-extract staging bundled runtime deps
              (1 missing, 29 install specs): pdfjs-dist@^5.6.205             ← npm install AFTER ready
14:49:03.880  [plugins] document-extract installed bundled runtime deps in 8700ms
14:49:12.863  [plugins] microsoft staging bundled runtime deps
              (1 missing, 30 install specs): node-edge-tts@^1.2.10           ← npm install AFTER ready
14:49:18.261  [plugins] microsoft installed bundled runtime deps in 5398ms
14:49:32       [last line of stdout — container SIGKILLed]
```

So:
- `[gateway] ready` fires at 14:48:39
- Two heavy bundled-plugin npm installs (`pdfjs-dist`, `node-edge-tts`) run from 14:48:55 → 14:49:18 — ~23 seconds of single-threaded Node.js event-loop pressure
- Container is `cpu: 500m` (half a core hard limit) so npm install gets CPU-throttled and stretches in wall-clock
- `/healthz` polls run on the same event loop → three consecutive timeouts → kubelet SIGKILL at ~14:49:32

The old pin `20260521.4` either announced `ready` AFTER bundled-plugin deps were resolved, or did not have these bundled-plugin runtime-install paths at all. Either way, the contract `gateway ready ⇒ /healthz responsive` was honored.

### Why this matters

1. **The sidecar pattern guarantees in Kubernetes are about probe responsiveness**, not internal readiness. `[gateway] ready` is meaningless to kubelet — only `/healthz` returning 200 within timeout matters. The current behavior breaks that contract.

2. **`bonjour` already shows event-loop starvation symptoms** in the same window (`service stuck in probing for 46498ms` between 14:46:39 and 14:47:25 — 46s of starvation on a single watchdog). So plugin runtime work is provably blocking the loop for tens of seconds at a stretch even pre-ready, and post-ready does it again.

3. **Bundled plugin deps shouldn't install at runtime in the request-serving process at all.** They should land at image-build time (the canonical path), or in an init container, or in a worker process — anywhere except the same event loop that serves `/healthz`.

### Reproduction

Stand up openclaw `20260604.2` as a Kubernetes sidecar with:
- `cpu: 500m` / `memory: 1536Mi` limits
- Liveness probe `httpGet :18789/healthz period=30s timeout=5s failure=3`
- Any agent config that loads the `document-extract` and `microsoft` plugins (default profile in nail-notes-api ai-central does this)
- Cold pod start (no `/home/node/.openclaw/plugins/...` cache from a prior pod)

Container dies with exit 137 in ~3-4 min, repeating every restart cycle. Backing the same configmap with pin `20260521.4` does not reproduce.

### Suggested fixes (pick one or stack)

**(A) Don't announce `ready` until bundled plugin deps install completes.** Simplest, preserves the contract. Cost: ~25s longer to first-serve on cold cache.

**(B) Move bundled-plugin runtime-dep install to a build-time / image-time step.** Cleanest long-term. `pdfjs-dist` and `node-edge-tts` are not user-facing config — they're bundled-by-default deps and should be on disk before the container starts.

**(C) Move bundled-plugin runtime-dep install into a worker thread / subprocess.** Preserves cold-start latency but adds plumbing.

**(D) Bump `livenessProbe.timeoutSeconds` / `failureThreshold` in the consumer.** Workaround only — papering over a real event-loop-starvation issue and the bonjour starvation evidence suggests this can happen at any time (not just during plugin install).

We're going to apply (D) as an emergency workaround on the ai-central deployment to get test cluster recovering today, but the openclaw-side fix should be (A) or (B). Happy to test patches against ai-central if a release candidate is cut.

### Related on consumer side

- nail-notes-api GH-5778 (https://github.com/smisy/nail-notes-api/issues/5778) — full diagnostic chain
- nail-notes-api GH-5768 — the pin bump that surfaced this

### Affected versions

- Bad: `nailnotesserviceacr.azurecr.io/openclaw:20260604.2` (upstream `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.4.26` base)
- Good: `nailnotesserviceacr.azurecr.io/openclaw:20260521.4`

Per the GH-5768 verification trail, the only changes between `20260521.4` and `20260604.2` in the upstream openclaw repo were GH-5562 (graphql-proxy nail-service routing) and GH-5585 (unrelated) — neither obviously touches plugin runtime-install or gateway-ready ordering. So the regression may actually be in a transitive bundled-plugin dep version bump that triggered the missing-runtime-dep `install_specs` path. Worth a `git log` on the document-extract and microsoft plugin manifests between the two tag dates.

cc @nails-cloud-system-design (consumer side / can repro + verify patches)
