No: current main and v2026.6.1 already suppress the Telegram empty-response fallback when the dispatch result is message-tool-only, including the zero-final/zero-delivery test shape. I did not run a live Telegram repro because this read-only review could prove the current source behavior directly.

Is this the best way to solve the issue?

Yes: the existing implementation is broader and cleaner than checking exact NO_REPLY after a successful send because it preserves the message_tool_only contract that final assistant text stays private and silence means no message-tool send.

ISSUE #90000: [Bug]: WhatsApp plugin incompatible with latest release 2026.5.28
Author: fedemengo
Date: 2026-06-03T20:35:15Z
Labels: P1, clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr, clawsweeper:needs-maintainer-review, clawsweeper:needs-product-decision, clawsweeper:source-repro, impact:auth-provider, issue-rating: 🦞 diamond lobster
State: closed

[c0]
## Bug type
Regression / release mismatch

## Summary
`openclaw 2026.5.28` is the latest release on GitHub, but the WhatsApp plugin cannot be installed or used on this version.

Installing or logging in with WhatsApp fails with:
- `Plugin "@openclaw/whatsapp" requires plugin API >=2026.6.1, but this OpenClaw runtime exposes 2026.5.28.`
- `Channel login failed: Error: Channel "whatsapp" does not support login.`

This blocks WhatsApp setup on the latest stable release.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Install or update to `openclaw 2026.5.28`
2. Run:
   ```bash
   openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp
   ```
   or try to install the plugin directly

## Expected behavior
WhatsApp should be installable and usable on the current latest release.

## Actual behavior
The WhatsApp plugin install fails due to an API version requirement mismatch, and the channel reports that login is unsupported.

## OpenClaw version
2026.5.28

## Operating system
macOS 15.6.1 x64

## Additional information
This looks related to the earlier WhatsApp regression in #52904, but the current failure is different: the latest stable release is published without a compatible WhatsApp plugin.

## Related issue
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/52904

I did not perform a live QR login or packaged CLI run.

Restore a stable-compatible WhatsApp install path by aligning the published ClawHub/npm dist-tags with OpenClaw 2026.5.28, promoting a compatible OpenClaw 2026.6.x release, or adding an official ClawHub incompatibility fallback to the existing npm compatible-version resolver.

I did not perform a live QR login or packaged CLI run.

Unclear until maintainers choose the release path. The best fix should preserve plugin API compatibility enforcement while aligning published package versions or adding a narrow official fallback to a compatible WhatsApp artifact.

title: EmbeddedPromptLockFileChangedError causes subagent announce to retry after message already delivered, resulting in duplicate messages
need_summary: Whether the duplicate subagent announcement retry problem is already fixed in released versions, with the answer anchored by merged PR #89812 and commit 79896a24d9bb941f7c9f3801a69f3ea01fb31043.
security_topic: duplicate message delivery after retry on post-send lock-file change
question_text: When a subagent completes and triggers an announce back to the requester session, if the main session file is concurrently being written (e.g., main agent is sending a Feishu message at the same moment), the announce throws `EmbeddedPromptLockFileChangedError` and retries — even though the message was already successfully delivered. This causes duplicate messages in the channel.
answer_text:
I found the merged PR that appears to have closed this: [#89812: fix(outbound): keep channel send durable when transcript mirror fails (#89626)](https://api.github.com/repos/openclaw/openclaw/pulls/89812).

So I’m closing this as already implemented rather than keeping a duplicate issue open.
thread_text:
ISSUE #89995: EmbeddedPromptLockFileChangedError causes subagent announce to retry after message already delivered, resulting in duplicate messages
Author: Nelsoncongbao
Date: 2026-06-03T20:19:58Z
Labels: P2, impact:message-loss
State: closed

[c0]
## Summary

When a subagent completes and triggers an announce back to the requester session, if the main session file is concurrently being written (e.g., main agent is sending a Feishu message at the same moment), the announce throws `EmbeddedPromptLockFileChangedError` and retries — even though the message was already successfully delivered. This causes duplicate messages in the channel.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Spawn a subagent via `sessions_spawn`
2. Subagent completes and triggers announce to main session
3. At the same moment, main agent is writing to the session file (e.g., delivering a reply to the user)
4. Announce throws `session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released`
5. Announce retries 3 times (5s / 10s / 20s intervals)
6. Each retry successfully sends the message → user receives 3 identical duplicate messages

## Log Evidence

```
feishu: sendText target=user:ou_xxx, textLength=25          ← message sent successfully
[warn] Subagent completion direct announce failed: text completion direct delivery failed: session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released: /path/to/session.jsonl
feishu: sendText target=user:ou_xxx, textLength=25          ← retry #1, duplicate sent
[warn] Subagent completion direct announce failed: ... session file changed ...
feishu: sendText target=user:ou_xxx, textLength=25          ← retry #2, duplicate sent
[warn] Subagent announce give up (retry-limit) run=xxx
```

## Root Cause

In `subagent-announce-delivery.js`, the error `session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released` (thrown as `EmbeddedPromptLockFileChangedError`) is **not classified** in either:
- `TRANSIENT_ANNOUNCE_DELIVERY_ERROR_PATTERNS` 
- `PERMANENT_ANNOUNCE_DELIVERY_ERROR_PATTERNS`

Despite this, the announce still retries. Critically, **no idempotency check is performed before retrying** — the code does not verify whether the message was already delivered before attempting to send again.

## Suggested Fix

Either:
1. Add `/session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released/i` to `PERMANENT_ANNOUNCE_DELIVERY_ERROR_PATTERNS` to prevent retry after this error
2. Record a delivery idempotency token when `sendText` succeeds, and check it before each retry to avoid duplicate delivery

## Environment

- OpenClaw version: 2026.6.1-beta.3 (3b53e2c)
- Channel: Feishu (via `@larksuite/openclaw-lark` plugin v2026.5.20)
- OS: Darwin 25.3.0 (arm64)
- Node: v24.14.1
- Reproducible: consistently, every subagent announce when main session has concurrent write activity

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @clawsweeper 2026-06-03T20:21:51Z:
Thanks for the context here. I did a careful shell check against current `main`, and this is already implemented.

Current main already fixes the reported duplicate-send path: outbound transcript mirror failures after a successful channel send are now warning-only, and the regression test uses the exact lock-change error from the report.

I found the merged PR that appears to have closed this: [#89812: fix(outbound): keep channel send durable when transcript mirror fails (#89626)](https://api.github.com/repos/openclaw/openclaw/pulls/89812).

So I’m closing this as already implemented rather than keeping a duplicate issue open.

<details>
<summary>Review details</summary>

Best possible solution:

Keep the current main implementation that treats post-send transcript mirror failures as non-fatal; users on older beta builds need a build containing 79896a24d9bb941f7c9f3801a69f3ea01fb31043.

Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue?

Yes, by source and regression-test evidence: pre-fix outbound delivery threw when the post-send transcript mirror failed with the exact lock-change message, and current main’s test now proves the channel send remains successful instead of retrying.

Is this the best way to solve the issue?

Yes; making transcript mirroring warning-only after platform send is the narrowest durable fix because it preserves the successful channel delivery and avoids duplicate retries without changing subagent retry policy or adding a new config surface.

Security review:

Security review: Non-PR issue triage; no patch security or supply-chain review applies.

AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant.

What I checked:

- **Repository policy read:** Full root AGENTS.md was read and applied, including the message-delivery, source/history/release-proof, and Codex-adjacent dependency-check guidance. ([`AGENTS.md:1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/a0717ef61c77/AGENTS.md#L1), [a0717ef61c77](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a0717ef61c77))
- **Current source keeps channel send successful after mirror failure:** After platform delivery succeeds, transcript mirroring is wrapped in warning-only handling so callers do not retry an already-sent channel payload. comments.author: Nelsoncongbao
comments.body:
## Summary

When a subagent completes and triggers an announce back to the requester session, if the main session file is concurrently being written (e.g., main agent is sending a Feishu message at the same moment), the announce throws `EmbeddedPromptLockFileChangedError` and retries — even though the message was already successfully delivered. This causes duplicate messages in the channel.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Spawn a subagent via `sessions_spawn`
2. Subagent completes and triggers announce to main session
3. At the same moment, main agent is writing to the session file (e.g., delivering a reply to the user)
4. Announce throws `session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released`
5. Announce retries 3 times (5s / 10s / 20s intervals)
6. Each retry successfully sends the message → user receives 3 identical duplicate messages

## Log Evidence

```
feishu: sendText target=user:ou_xxx, textLength=25          ← message sent successfully
[warn] Subagent completion direct announce failed: text completion direct delivery failed: session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released: /path/to/session.jsonl
feishu: sendText target=user:ou_xxx, textLength=25          ← retry #1, duplicate sent
[warn] Subagent completion direct announce failed: ... session file changed ...
feishu: sendText target=user:ou_xxx, textLength=25          ← retry #2, duplicate sent
[warn] Subagent announce give up (retry-limit) run=xxx
```

## Root Cause

In `subagent-announce-delivery.js`, the error `session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released` (thrown as `EmbeddedPromptLockFileChangedError`) is **not classified** in either:
- `TRANSIENT_ANNOUNCE_DELIVERY_ERROR_PATTERNS` 
- `PERMANENT_ANNOUNCE_DELIVERY_ERROR_PATTERNS`

Despite this, the announce still retries. Critically, **no idempotency check is performed before retrying** — the code does not verify whether the message was already delivered before attempting to send again.

## Suggested Fix

Either:
1. Add `/session file changed while embedded prompt lock was released/i` to `PERMANENT_ANNOUNCE_DELIVERY_ERROR_PATTERNS` to prevent retry after this error
2. Record a delivery idempotency token when `sendText` succeeds, and check it before each retry to avoid duplicate delivery

## Environment

- OpenClaw version: 2026.6.1-beta.3 (3b53e2c)
- Channel: Feishu (via `@larksuite/openclaw-lark` plugin v2026.5.20)
- OS: Darwin 25.3.0 (arm64)
- Node: v24.14.1
- Reproducible: consistently, every subagent announce when main session has concurrent write activity

ISSUE #89881: Memory flush via suppressNextUserMessagePersistence bypasses write-tool append-only wrapping — daily memory silently overwritten (still present in v2026.5.28, commit e932160)
Author: bizzle12368239
Date: 2026-06-03T15:02:11Z
Labels: P2, impact:data-loss
State: closed

[c0]
## Summary

When a user message arrives with `suppressNextUserMessagePersistence: true`, the runtime injects a synthetic memory-flush prompt (`"Continue the OpenClaw runtime event."`) into the embedded agent run. On this code path, the `write` tool is **not** wrapped with `wrapToolMemoryFlushAppendOnlyWrite`, so a model that calls `write` on the daily memory file silently **replaces the entire file** instead of appending. The previous closure of #89195 as "already implemented in v2026.5.28" did not address this path — the bug remains reproducible in v2026.5.28 (commit e932160).

## Affected versions

- v2026.5.27 — confirmed reproduced
- v2026.5.28 (commit e932160) — confirmed still present via dist inspection

## Reproduction conditions

1. Pre-compaction message arrives carrying `suppressNextUserMessagePersistence: true`
2. Runtime selects `emptyTranscriptMode: "model-prompt"` in `dist/selection-*.js` (line ~16823):
   ```js
   emptyTranscriptMode: params.suppressNextUserMessagePersistence ? "model-prompt" : "runtime-event"
   ```
3. Embedded agent is invoked via the runtime-context prompt in `dist/runtime-context-prompt-*.js`:
   ```js
   const OPENCLAW_RUNTIME_EVENT_USER_PROMPT = "Continue the OpenClaw runtime event.";
   ```
4. Because this path does **not** set `trigger: "memory"`, the condition in `dist/agent-tools-*.js` (line ~2003) evaluates to `false`:
   ```js
   const isMemoryFlushRun = options?.trigger === "memory";
   ```
5. The write-tool wrapping block (lines ~2399–2410) is skipped:
   ```js
   const toolsForMemoryFlush = isMemoryFlushRun && memoryFlushWritePath ? [] : tools;
   if (isMemoryFlushRun && memoryFlushWritePath) for (const tool of tools) { ... }
   ```
6. A model calling `write` with the daily memory file path overwrites the file in full. No error, no log.

## Observed impact

On v2026.5.27, a single compaction event reduced a daily memory file from 22,897 characters to 659 characters across three `write` calls. The model was completing a memory flush, the file existed, and `write` replaced the entire content with only the flush summary.

## Suggested fix

Apply the append-only write wrapper to the suppress path. Two reasonable shapes:

1. Extend the `isMemoryFlushRun` check in `agent-tools-*.js` to also cover `options?.emptyTranscriptMode === "model-prompt"` (or whatever flag tracks the suppress-path memory flush), so the existing `wrapToolMemoryFlushAppendOnlyWrite` block fires for both paths.

2. Have the runtime-context-prompt code pass `trigger: "memory"` through to the embedded agent run when the underlying operation is a memory flush, so Path A and Path B share the same wrapping gate.

## Related

- #89195 — original report (closed as "already implemented in v2026.5.28" without checking Path B)
- #89205 — narrower follow-up on the same `suppressNextUserMessagePersistence` path; also closed
- `dist/selection-*.js` — `emptyTranscriptMode` routing decision
- `dist/runtime-context-prompt-*.js` — `OPENCLAW_RUNTIME_EVENT_USER_PROMPT` constant
- `dist/agent-tools-*.js` — `isMemoryFlushRun` gating and `wrapToolMemoryFlushAppendOnlyWrite` application

comments.body:
## Summary

When a user message arrives with `suppressNextUserMessagePersistence: true`, the runtime injects a synthetic memory-flush prompt (`"Continue the OpenClaw runtime event."`) into the embedded agent run. On this code path, the `write` tool is **not** wrapped with `wrapToolMemoryFlushAppendOnlyWrite`, so a model that calls `write` on the daily memory file silently **replaces the entire file** instead of appending. The previous closure of #89195 as "already implemented in v2026.5.28" did not address this path — the bug remains reproducible in v2026.5.28 (commit e932160).

## Affected versions

- v2026.5.27 — confirmed reproduced
- v2026.5.28 (commit e932160) — confirmed still present via dist inspection

## Reproduction conditions

1. Pre-compaction message arrives carrying `suppressNextUserMessagePersistence: true`
2. Runtime selects `emptyTranscriptMode: "model-prompt"` in `dist/selection-*.js` (line ~16823):
   ```js
   emptyTranscriptMode: params.suppressNextUserMessagePersistence ? "model-prompt" : "runtime-event"
   ```
3. Embedded agent is invoked via the runtime-context prompt in `dist/runtime-context-prompt-*.js`:
   ```js
   const OPENCLAW_RUNTIME_EVENT_USER_PROMPT = "Continue the OpenClaw runtime event.";
   ```
4. Because this path does **not** set `trigger: "memory"`, the condition in `dist/agent-tools-*.js` (line ~2003) evaluates to `false`:
   ```js
   const isMemoryFlushRun = options?.trigger === "memory";
   ```
5. The write-tool wrapping block (lines ~2399–2410) is skipped:
   ```js
   const toolsForMemoryFlush = isMemoryFlushRun && memoryFlushWritePath ? [] : tools;
   if (isMemoryFlushRun && memoryFlushWritePath) for (const tool of tools) { ... }
   ```
6. A model calling `write` with the daily memory file path overwrites the file in full. No error, no log.

## Observed impact

On v2026.5.27, a single compaction event reduced a daily memory file from 22,897 characters to 659 characters across three `write` calls. The model was completing a memory flush, the file existed, and `write` replaced the entire content with only the flush summary.

## Suggested fix

Apply the append-only write wrapper to the suppress path. Two reasonable shapes:

1. Extend the `isMemoryFlushRun` check in `agent-tools-*.js` to also cover `options?.emptyTranscriptMode === "model-prompt"` (or whatever flag tracks the suppress-path memory flush), so the existing `wrapToolMemoryFlushAppendOnlyWrite` block fires for both paths.

2. Have the runtime-context-prompt code pass `trigger: "memory"` through to the embedded agent run when the underlying operation is a memory flush, so Path A and Path B share the same wrapping gate.

## Related

- #89195 — original report (closed as "already implemented in v2026.5.28" without checking Path B)
- #89205 — narrower follow-up on the same `suppressNextUserMessagePersistence` path; also closed
- `dist/selection-*.js` — `emptyTranscriptMode` routing decision
- `dist/runtime-context-prompt-*.js` — `OPENCLAW_RUNTIME_EVENT_USER_PROMPT` constant
- `dist/agent-tools-*.js` — `isMemoryFlushRun` gating and `wrapToolMemoryFlushAppendOnlyWrite` application

comments.body:
Thanks for the context here. I did a careful shell check against current `main`, and this is already implemented.

Close: current main and the v2026.5.28 release source already route memory-triggered flush runs through append-only write wrapping; the cited suppress flag is a generic transcript-persistence mode, not the memory-flush guard boundary.

So I’m closing this as already implemented rather than keeping a duplicate issue open.

<details>
<summary>Review details</summary>

Best possible solution:

Keep the explicit `trigger: "memory"` plus `memoryFlushWritePath` guard and avoid broadening memory tool policy to generic suppressed transcript retries.

Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue?

No. Source inspection shows current main's pre-compaction memory flush path reaches tool construction with `trigger: "memory"` and `memoryFlushWritePath`, and the tests cover append-only behavior rather than a failing current-main path.

Is this the best way to solve the issue?

Yes. The current implementation uses explicit memory-flush metadata as the maintainable boundary; using `suppressNextUserMessagePersistence` alone would apply memory-write restrictions to unrelated suppressed retry and room-event turns.

Security review:

Security review: No patch is under review; this is issue triage for an already-guarded memory data-safety path.

AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant.

What I checked:

- **Current source: memory flush run carries guard metadata:** The silent memory flush path calls the embedded agent with `trigger: "memory"`, `memoryFlushWritePath`, and an empty transcript prompt, so the run is identifiable to tool construction. ([`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.ts:1247`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e0ab71d3dcf1/src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.ts#L1247), [e0ab71d3dcf1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e0ab71d3dcf1))

([`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.tool-run-context.ts:21`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e0ab71d3dcf1/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.tool-run-context.ts#L21), [e0ab71d3dcf1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e0ab71d3dcf1))

([`src/agents/agent-tools.ts:1039`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e0ab71d3dcf1/src/agents/agent-tools.ts#L1039), [e0ab71d3dcf1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e0ab71d3dcf1))

([`src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts:630`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e0ab71d3dcf1/src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts#L630), [e0ab71d3dcf1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e0ab71d3dcf1))
